item.title: Airline Sentiment Analysis: Interactive Exploration with Streamlit
item.description:
Executive summary

This case study describes an interactive Streamlit app for exploring tweets about airlines, grouped by positive, negative and neutral sentiment. Users can inspect sentiment distributions, filter by time and location, compare airlines and explore frequently used terms.

The project focuses on exploratory analysis and visualization of sentiment-labeled tweets. The original article does not document training or evaluating a new sentiment classification model. Its use of a tweet dataset should not be confused with verified real-time social media ingestion.

item.title: Building a Python ETL Pipeline: Unifying CSV, JSON and XML Data
item.description:
Executive summary

This project demonstrates a straightforward Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) workflow written in Python. It consolidates records stored in CSV, JSON and XML files into a consistent dataset and produces two artifacts: transformed_data.csv and log_file.txt.

The case study focuses on the core engineering considerations behind the implementation: heterogeneous inputs, standardization rules, repeatable execution and traceability through logs. It is a small-scale educational pipeline, rather than a production platform.
